title: Harden untrusted image input handling
description: The only meaningful attack surface in this tool is decoding image files that may be attacker-supplied: HEIC/JPEG/PNG decoders are a historically rich source of CVEs and decompression-bomb denial of service. Verify and lock in the defensive posture — keep Pillow's decompression-bomb guard active, fail cleanly on malformed input, and confirm no path-traversal or metadata-leak surface exists.
acceptanceCriteria: `Image.MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS` is never raised or set to None anywhere in the codebase (verified by grep)
A `DecompressionBombError`/`DecompressionBombWarning` from Pillow surfaces as a clean `ValueError` from `load_rgb`, not a crash or a silent oversized allocation
A truncated/corrupt file of each supported format raises `ValueError` with the path in the message, not a raw PIL exception
`ImageFile.LOAD_TRUNCATED_IMAGES` is left at its default False so truncated files fail rather than decode partially
No output is ever written outside the target image's parent directory, verified by a test using a target path containing `..`
No EXIF, GPS, or ICC data from either input appears in the output file (regression test on top of TASK-8's check)
The tool performs zero network I/O (verified by a test that fails if `socket.socket` is instantiated during a run)
A short `Security` section is added to the README covering these properties

steps.details: Grep the codebase for `MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS` and `LOAD_TRUNCATED_IMAGES`. Both must be absent. Add a comment in `io_image.py` stating explicitly that Pillow's decompression-bomb limit is intentionally left at its default and must not be raised, so a future contributor does not 'fix' a bomb warning by disabling the guard.

steps.description: Convert bomb warnings into clean failures
steps.details: In `load_rgb`, wrap the open/decode in `warnings.catch_warnings()` with `simplefilter('error', Image.DecompressionBombWarning)` so the warning becomes an exception, and catch both `Image.DecompressionBombWarning` and `Image.DecompressionBombError` in the existing except clause, re-raising as `ValueError(f'refusing to decode {path}: image too large')`.

In `tests/test_security.py`, monkeypatch `Image.MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS` to a very small value (e.g. 100) for the duration of one test, then call `load_rgb` on a normal 128x192 PNG. Assert `ValueError` is raised and its message mentions the path. Restore the original value via the monkeypatch fixture. This tests the handling without needing to create an actual gigapixel file.

steps.description: Test malformed input for each format
steps.details: For each of `.png`, `.jpg`, `.heic`: write a file containing the correct magic-byte prefix followed by random bytes, plus a file that is a valid image truncated to its first 40 bytes. Assert `load_rgb` raises `ValueError` (not `OSError`, `UnidentifiedImageError`, or a segfault) and that the message contains the path.

Create a target at `tmp_path / 'sub' / 'photo.png'` and call `resolve_outputs` with a path expressed as `tmp_path / 'sub' / '..' / 'sub' / 'photo.png'`. Assert both returned paths, after `.resolve()`, are inside `tmp_path / 'sub'`. This confirms outputs always land beside the target and cannot be redirected by a crafted path.

Build a JPEG carrying EXIF with a GPS tag and a fabricated ICC profile using Pillow. Run the full pipeline with it as the target. Reopen the output and assert `getexif()` contains no GPS tags and `img.info.get('icc_profile')` is None. This is a privacy property, so it deserves its own regression test independent of TASK-8.

Use monkeypatch to replace `socket.socket` with a function that raises `AssertionError('network access attempted')`, then run a full `match_luminance`. The run must complete successfully, proving the tool is fully offline and cannot exfiltrate image data.

Add a `Security` section to the README (or a placeholder to be folded into TASK-26) listing: no network I/O, no credentials or environment variables, decompression-bomb guard active, source metadata stripped from output, outputs confined to the target's directory, and a note to keep Pillow and pillow-heif updated because decoder CVEs are the real risk.
Run `.venv/bin/pytest tests/test_security.py -q`, then the full suite, then `.venv/bin/ruff check src tests`.

technicalNotes: Monkeypatching MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS down is far better than generating a real decompression bomb — same code path, no multi-GB test fixture.

The most likely real-world vulnerability here is a libheif CVE, which no amount of application code can mitigate. Keeping dependencies current is the actual control, which is why it goes in the README rather than the code.
Normalizing every decoder failure to ValueError matters for the CLI contract: TASK-18 maps ValueError to a clean exit 2, so a leaked PIL exception type would produce an ugly traceback instead.
The no-network test also documents intent: if someone later adds telemetry or a remote model call, this test fails immediately.
